title: WPSS/1632/2019 of HARISH CHANDRA JOSHI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPSS No. 1632 of 2019
Hon 'b le Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.

Mr. Shivanand Bhatt, Advocate for
the petitioner.
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Additional C.S.C. and
Mr. Sushil Vashishta, Standing Counsel
for the State of Uttarakhand.
Heard learned counsel for the
parties.
Petitioner is a physically disabled
person as defined under Rights of
Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. He
was appointed on a Group 'D' post in
School Education Department. Group 'D'
em ployees of Education Department are
eligible to be considered for promotion to
Group 'C' post of Junior Clerk, however,
for such prom otion, a person has to
qualify in written examination. Petitioner
participated in the written examination,
however, he was not prom oted,
therefore, he has filed this writ petition,
seeking the following relief:
"I . I ssue a writ order or direction in the
nature of Mandamus directing the respondents to
grant the promotion to the petitioner under 3%
reservation meant for disabled persons as provided
in G.O. dated 14.6.2018."
I n sum & substance, contention of
the petitioner is that since he is a person
with disability, therefore, he is entitled to
benefit available to disabled persons in
term s of provision contained in Rights of
Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.
Thus, according to petitioner, the said
statutory right has been denied to the
petitioner, inasm uch as, benefit of

reservation has not been given to him .
A counter affidavit has been filed by
Mrs. Sahista Jam al Ansari, Principal,
G.G.I.C. Pantnagar, Udham Singh Nagar.
Paragraph no. 4 of the said counter
affidavit is reproduced below:
"4. That the contents of para no. 9 of the writ
petition are matter of record, hence needs no reply.
However, it is subm itted that petitioner appeared in
the written and typing examination held for the
promotion from Group D to Group C post. Written
examination was held on 13.10.2018 and typing
examination was held from 16.01.2019 to
19.01.2019. The petitioner was failed in typing
examination, therefore the petitioner could not get
promotion from Group D post to Group C i.e. clerical
cadre post."
No rejoinder affidavit has been filed
by the petitioner. Thus, this Court has
no other option but to treat the
averment m ade in paragraph no. 4 to be
true.
Since petitioner appeared in the
written examination of qualifying nature
for prom otion to Group 'C' post of Junior
Clerk and failed, therefore, grievance
raised by the petitioner is without any
substance. There is nothing in the
relevant recruitm ent Rules, which
provides for relaxation in requirem ent of
passing the qualifying test for the
physically disabled persons.
I n such view of the m atter, there is
no scope for interference.
Accordingly, the writ petition fails
and is dismissed.

( Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.)
